summary:
I have always wondered about the kind of person who will often approach you with this sort of statement, “There’s something I feel I should tell you but it might hurt you. Do you want me to be honest? Do you want me to tell you the truth and be frank with you?” Naturally, what can you say? You can hardly say, “No, I want you to lie and say something nice.” When they put it this way they have you. But what they call “honesty” or “frankness” is actually a cruelty or an 
overt power-play at your expense, masquerading under these self-serving terms. “Do you want me to tell you the truth?” is in effect an opening wedge in which a power-oriented person or else an outright sadistic person, or both combined, gains a tactical advantage over you even more and more. It usually begins like this, and as a big name writer I have had it tried on me again and again, usually with a fair amount of success. I find it manifesting itself frequently in persons who hithertofore have presented themselves as reasonably warm and friendly. But then the mask comes off and the naked fist of tyranny is revealed. Your motivation, Sherry, for telling me blatantly to my face that “Fog” is, in your words, “...crude satire and virtually worthless,” after previously telling me (I refer to your previous letter) “‘Fog’ is the perfect imagistic poem, which Carl Sandburg and others strove after but never attained,” which I sensed at the time as possessing a certain rather overdone unctuous quality, can be detected ...
